en: Chlorophyll in plant leaves absorbs sunlight energy to convert water and carbon dioxide into glucose for food and oxygen.
The stomach secretes hydrochloric acid and enzymes to break down solid food into a liquid mixture called chyme.
The leaf-tailed gecko's flattened tail and mottled skin pattern perfectly mimic tree bark to hide from predators.
When sea otters eat sea urchins, they prevent the urchins from overgrazing and destroying vital kelp forest ecosystems.
The right ventricle pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs, where it releases carbon dioxide and absorbs fresh oxygen.
Plant roots grow downward due to gravitropism, where specialized cells detect gravity and direct root growth toward the soil.
Inside a chrysalis, enzymes completely dissolve a caterpillar's tissues into a nutrient-rich liquid before rebuilding them into an adult butterfly.
Dogs pant to evaporate moisture from their tongues and lungs, which cools their blood and lowers body temperature.
Vaccines introduce weakened pathogens to the body, prompting white blood cells to produce specific antibodies that remember future infections.
Trees absorb groundwater through their roots and release it as water vapor through leaf stomata in a process called transpiration.
Sensory neurons detect heat from a hot stove and send electrical signals to the brain, triggering muscles to pull the hand away.
Bees collect nectar from flowers, and the sticky pollen attached to their bodies transfers to other flowers to enable plant reproduction.
